properties.name: egradx.audit.retention.default-period

properties.name: egradx.auth.account.email-change-resend-interval

properties.name: egradx.auth.account.invitation-ttl

properties.name: egradx.auth.account.password-reset-resend-interval

properties.name: egradx.auth.account.password-reset-ttl
properties.description: How long a password-reset link works.

properties.name: egradx.auth.cleanup.enabled
properties.description: Run the clean-up on this instance.

properties.name: egradx.auth.cleanup.interval
properties.description: How often the clean-up runs.

properties.name: egradx.auth.default-admin-role-name
properties.description:
The name of the role every organization is guaranteed to have. egradx-auth creates it whenever an organization is created — including the platform organization — and seeds it with {@link com.egradx.auth.EgradxAuthorities#ORGANIZATION_ADMIN}, so a brand-new organization always has someone who can administer it.

A host app adds its own default roles on top by listening for {@code EgradxOrganizationCreatedEvent} — one app's tenants might additionally start with Manager/Staff, another's with teaching-staff/administrative-staff. Only this one is the SDK's.

properties.name: egradx.auth.email-code.enabled
properties.description: Offer signing in with an emailed code. Needs something that delivers account messages.

properties.name: egradx.auth.email-code.max-attempts
properties.description: Wrong codes allowed before a new one must be asked for.

properties.name: egradx.auth.email-code.resend-interval
properties.description: How soon another code may be sent to the same address.

properties.name: egradx.auth.email-code.ttl
properties.description: How long a code works.

properties.name: egradx.auth.issuer-uri
properties.description: The {@code iss} claim egradx-auth stamps on every token it issues, and requires when verifying one. Since tokens are both issued and verified locally by this same app (no external authorization server), this can be any stable identifier for the app — it does not need to be a resolvable URL.

properties.name: egradx.auth.links.base-url
properties.description: The frontend's public origin, e.g. {@code https://app.example.com}.

properties.name: egradx.auth.links.invitation-path
properties.description: Where invitation emails link to, after the base URL; {@code {token}} is replaced with the token.

properties.name: egradx.auth.links.password-reset-path
properties.description: {@code {token}} is replaced with the (URL-encoded) token.

properties.name: egradx.auth.oidc.callback-base-url
properties.description: This server's public address as the provider's browser redirect reaches it, e.g. {@code https://api.example.com/api}. A provider's redirect URI is this plus {@code /egradx/auth/oidc/{id}/callback}; register it with the provider.

properties.name: egradx.auth.oidc.flow-ttl
properties.description: How long a round trip to a provider, and the code it ends with, may take.

properties.name: egradx.auth.oidc.frontend-callback-path
properties.description: Where on the frontend (after {@code links.base-url}) the browser lands after the provider.

properties.name: egradx.auth.oidc.providers
properties.description: The providers, by id ({@code google}, {@code zoho}, …): the id is in the URLs and on the buttons' data.

properties.name: egradx.auth.oidc.providers.<id>.client-id
properties.description: The client id the provider issued for this application. Without it the provider is left out, with a warning.

properties.name: egradx.auth.oidc.providers.<id>.client-secret
properties.description: The client secret the provider issued for this application. Without it the provider is left out, with a warning.

properties.name: egradx.auth.oidc.providers.<id>.enabled
properties.description: Turn the provider off without removing its settings.

properties.name: egradx.auth.oidc.providers.<id>.issuer
properties.description: The provider's issuer; its discovery document is at {@code {issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration}. Required for {@code type: oidc}.

properties.name: egradx.auth.oidc.providers.<id>.name
properties.description: Shown on the button. Defaults to the type's name ({@code Google}, {@code Zoho}), else the id.

properties.name: egradx.auth.oidc.providers.<id>.scopes
properties.description: Scopes asked for.

properties.name: egradx.auth.oidc.providers.<id>.trust-email
properties.description: Take the provider's verified emails as proof of owning the address: a sign-in whose email matches an account is linked to it. Defaults to true for the google and zoho types and false otherwise.

properties.name: egradx.auth.oidc.providers.<id>.type
properties.description: What kind of provider, so which EgradxSignInProviderFactory makes it: {@code oidc} (any OpenID Connect provider, from its issuer), {@code google}, {@code zoho}, or a type an application adds with an {@code EgradxSignInProviderFactory} bean. {@code google} and {@code zoho} fill in the issuer, the name and {@code trust-email}.

properties.name: egradx.auth.platform.admin-display-name
properties.description: The platform administrator's display name, used when the account is created.

properties.name: egradx.auth.platform.admin-email
properties.description: The platform administrator's email, used when the account is created.

properties.name: egradx.auth.platform.admin-password
properties.description: Only used the first time the platform admin is created; changing it later does not reset the password. egradx-auth logs a warning at startup while this is left at its default, since a known password on the account that can administer every organization is the single worst credential to leave unchanged.

properties.name: egradx.auth.platform.admin-username
properties.description: The platform administrator's username, used when the account is created.

properties.name: egradx.auth.platform.enabled
properties.description: Set false if the host app seeds the platform organization itself.

properties.name: egradx.auth.platform.organization-name
properties.description: The platform organization's name, used when it is created.

properties.name: egradx.auth.profile.channels
properties.description: The channels a person can add an address for — the same ids egradx-notification uses. {@code email}, {@code sms}, {@code whatsapp} and {@code slack} have their formats checked; any other id accepts any address.

properties.name: egradx.auth.profile.max-attribute-value-length
properties.description: Characters per further-detail value.

properties.name: egradx.auth.profile.max-attributes
properties.description: Further-detail entries per profile.

properties.name: egradx.auth.profile.max-contacts
properties.description: Contact addresses per person, in all organizations together.

properties.name: egradx.auth.profile.verification-code-ttl
properties.description: How long a code verifying an address works.

properties.name: egradx.auth.profile.verification-max-attempts
properties.description: Wrong codes allowed before a new one must be requested.

properties.name: egradx.auth.profile.verification-resend-interval
properties.description: How soon another code may be requested for the same address.

properties.name: egradx.auth.rate-limit.enabled
properties.description: Limit sign-in attempts.

properties.name: egradx.auth.rate-limit.max-failures-per-account
properties.description: Failures allowed for one account from one address within {@link #window}.

properties.name: egradx.auth.rate-limit.max-failures-per-address
properties.description: Failures allowed from one address, across all accounts, within {@link #window}.

properties.name: egradx.auth.rate-limit.max-tracked
properties.description: Accounts and addresses tracked at once; beyond it, the least recently seen are forgotten.

properties.name: egradx.auth.rate-limit.window
properties.description: How far back failures count. The wait is until the oldest counted failure leaves it.

properties.name: egradx.auth.refresh-token-reuse-grace-seconds
properties.description: How long a refresh token replaced by a refresh still renews its session, in seconds, so that two callers refreshing with it at once (two tabs, a page and its route handler) both carry on. Presented after this, it ends the session as a stolen copy.

properties.name: egradx.auth.refresh-token-ttl-days
properties.description: How long a session lasts, in days: its refresh tokens stop working this long after sign-in, however often they rotate.

properties.name: egradx.auth.role-authorities-cache-ttl-seconds
properties.description: How long a role's resolved authority set stays cached ({@code egradx-role-authorities}, an in-process Caffeine cache by default) before falling back to the database even without an explicit edit having evicted it — a fleet-wide safety net alongside the precise, immediate eviction that a role edit itself triggers, in case more than one instance of the host app is running (each with its own in-process cache, only one of which gets the explicit eviction).

properties.name: egradx.auth.schema.migrate
properties.description: Off: create the tables yourself from {@code db/egradx-auth/postgresql/} in this jar.

properties.name: egradx.auth.signup.allowed-email-domains
properties.description: Email domains allowed to sign up ({@code example.com}); empty allows any.

properties.name: egradx.auth.signup.legacy-register
properties.description: Keep the deprecated {@code POST /egradx/auth/register}, which makes an account in no organization. Off, it answers {@code SIGNUP_DISABLED}.

properties.name: egradx.auth.signup.mode
properties.description: {@code invitation}: accounts are made only by an administrator or by accepting an invitation. {@code organization}: anyone may also sign up, and becomes the administrator of a new organization of their own. Joining an existing organization always takes an invitation.

properties.name: egradx.errors.fallback.enabled
properties.description: Whether failures on the application's own endpoints that no advice of its own answers are answered in the EGRADX error envelope. An advice of the application's own answers first either way; set false to leave every unanswered failure to Spring Boot.

properties.name: egradx.events.enabled
properties.description: Off: no publisher, no handlers called, no tables.

properties.name: egradx.events.kafka.bootstrap-servers
properties.description: Default: {@code spring.kafka.bootstrap-servers}.

properties.name: egradx.events.kafka.concurrency
properties.description: Consumer threads per instance.

properties.name: egradx.events.kafka.group-id
properties.description: This service's consumer group. Default: the source.

properties.name: egradx.events.kafka.max-deliveries
properties.description: Deliveries of one event before it goes to the dead-letter topic, {@code <topic>.DLT}.

properties.name: egradx.events.kafka.send-timeout
properties.description: How long a send waits for the broker to acknowledge it.

properties.name: egradx.events.kafka.topic-prefix
properties.description: Put before each event type to make its topic name.

properties.name: egradx.events.rabbitmq.concurrency
properties.description: Consumers of this service's queue, per instance.

properties.name: egradx.events.rabbitmq.confirm-timeout
properties.description: How long a send waits for the broker to confirm it.

properties.name: egradx.events.rabbitmq.delivery-limit
properties.description: Deliveries of one event before it goes to the queue's dead-letter queue.

properties.name: egradx.events.rabbitmq.exchange
properties.description: The topic exchange every service publishes to.

properties.name: egradx.events.rabbitmq.queue
properties.description: This service's queue. Default: {@code egradx.events.<source>}.

properties.name: egradx.events.rabbitmq.retry-delay
properties.description: How long a failed event waits in the queue's retry queue before it is delivered again.

properties.name: egradx.events.relay.batch-size
properties.description: Events claimed from the outbox per pass.

properties.name: egradx.events.relay.first-retry
properties.description: The wait after the first failed send; it doubles after each, up to {@link #maxRetry}.

properties.name: egradx.events.relay.keep-handled
properties.description: How long the inbox remembers a handled event: longer than any broker could take to deliver it again.

properties.name: egradx.events.relay.keep-sent
properties.description: How long sent events stay in the outbox.

properties.name: egradx.events.relay.lease
properties.description: How long a claimed row is left to the instance that claimed it.

properties.name: egradx.events.relay.max-attempts
properties.description: Attempts at sending one event before it is marked dead.

properties.name: egradx.events.relay.max-retry
properties.description: The longest wait between two attempts at sending one event.

properties.name: egradx.events.relay.poll-interval
properties.description: How often the outbox is looked at when nothing wakes the relay.

properties.name: egradx.events.schema.migrate
properties.description: The library creates and migrates its tables. Off: create them from db/egradx-events/postgresql/ yourself.

properties.name: egradx.events.source
properties.description: The service events come from (CloudEvents' {@code source}). Default: {@code spring.application.name}.

properties.name: egradx.events.transport
properties.description: How events travel: {@code in-process}, {@code rabbitmq} or {@code kafka}.

properties.name: egradx.files.allowed-content-types
properties.description: Content types that may be uploaded, such as {@code image/*} or {@code application/pdf}; empty allows any.

properties.name: egradx.files.backend
properties.description: Where the bytes are stored: {@code local} (a folder) or {@code s3} (any S3-compatible store).

properties.name: egradx.files.cleanup.enabled
properties.description: Run the clean-up on this instance.

properties.name: egradx.files.cleanup.interval
properties.description: How often it runs.

properties.name: egradx.files.local.root
properties.description: The folder files are stored in; created if missing. With several instances, a folder they all share.

properties.name: egradx.files.max-size
properties.description: The largest file that may be uploaded. Spring's multipart limits are raised to fit it.

properties.name: egradx.files.profile-photo.content-types
properties.description: Content types a profile photo may have.

properties.name: egradx.files.profile-photo.max-size
properties.description: The largest profile photo.

properties.name: egradx.files.s3.access-key
properties.description: The access key; without it, the AWS SDK's default credentials are used.

properties.name: egradx.files.s3.bucket
properties.description: The bucket files are stored in; it must exist.

properties.name: egradx.files.s3.endpoint
properties.description: The store's address, for anything but AWS itself, e.g. {@code http://localhost:9000} for MinIO.

properties.name: egradx.files.s3.path-style
properties.description: Address the bucket in the path rather than the host name; most S3-compatible stores need it.

properties.name: egradx.files.s3.presigned-downloads
properties.description: Downloads redirect (302) to a short-lived pre-signed URL instead of streaming through the application.

properties.name: egradx.files.s3.presigned-ttl
properties.description: How long a pre-signed download URL works.

properties.name: egradx.files.s3.region
properties.description: The region; any value for most S3-compatible stores.

properties.name: egradx.files.s3.secret-key
properties.description: The secret key, with {@code access-key}.

properties.name: egradx.files.schema.migrate
properties.description: Off: create the table yourself from {@code db/egradx-file-storage/postgresql/} in this jar.

properties.name: egradx.notification.bulk.max-recipients
properties.description: The largest audience a bulk send may reach, checked before anything is queued. Low by default, so that a mistaken call cannot mass-message a platform. Raise it deliberately.

properties.name: egradx.notification.bulk.page-size
properties.description: Recipients expanded into deliveries per transaction.

properties.name: egradx.notification.channels.log.enabled
properties.description: Offer the log channel. Off by default: it writes message bodies to the log.

properties.name: egradx.notification.channels.slack.enabled
properties.description: Offer the Slack channel.

properties.name: egradx.notification.channels.sms.enabled
properties.description: Offer the SMS channel.

properties.name: egradx.notification.channels.webhook.allow-http
properties.description: Accept plain {@code http://} addresses. For local development only.

properties.name: egradx.notification.channels.webhook.enabled
properties.description: Offer the webhook channel.

properties.name: egradx.notification.channels.whatsapp.enabled
properties.description: Offer the WhatsApp channel.

properties.name: egradx.notification.dispatcher.backoff.initial
properties.description: The wait before the first retry.

properties.name: egradx.notification.dispatcher.backoff.jitter
properties.description: Fraction of each delay to randomise by, from 0 (none) to 1.

properties.name: egradx.notification.dispatcher.backoff.max
properties.description: The longest wait between retries.

properties.name: egradx.notification.dispatcher.backoff.multiplier
properties.description: What each wait is multiplied by for the next.

properties.name: egradx.notification.dispatcher.batch-size
properties.description: Deliveries claimed per round trip. They are sent concurrently, each on its own virtual thread.

properties.name: egradx.notification.dispatcher.enabled
properties.description: Whether this instance delivers messages. Instances with this off still accept {@code submit}; their messages are delivered by whichever instances have it on. Useful for dedicating delivery to worker instances as load grows.

properties.name: egradx.notification.dispatcher.lease
properties.description: How long a claimed delivery stays hidden from other dispatchers. If this instance dies mid-send, the delivery becomes due again after this long. Must exceed {@link #sendTimeout}.

properties.name: egradx.notification.dispatcher.max-attempts
properties.description: Attempts before a retryable failure becomes {@code DEAD}, the first attempt included.

properties.name: egradx.notification.dispatcher.poll-interval
properties.description: How often to look for due deliveries when idle. A submit on this instance wakes the dispatcher immediately after its transaction commits, so this mostly bounds how quickly retries, and messages submitted on other instances, are picked up.

properties.name: egradx.notification.dispatcher.send-timeout
properties.description: How long a batch waits for its sends. A send still running after this is abandoned, and its delivery is retried once the lease lapses.

properties.name: egradx.notification.email.from
properties.description: The sender address.

properties.name: egradx.notification.email.from-name
properties.description: The sender's display name.

properties.name: egradx.notification.email.reply-to
properties.description: The Reply-To address, if any.

properties.name: egradx.notification.inbox.heartbeat
properties.description: A comment sent on every open stream this often, inside a typical proxy's idle window.

properties.name: egradx.notification.inbox.max-connections-per-user
properties.description: Open streams one user may hold on one instance; opening another closes the oldest.

properties.name: egradx.notification.inbox.stream-timeout
properties.description: How long a stream stays open before the client must reconnect.

properties.name: egradx.notification.max-attachment-bytes-per-message
properties.description: The most attachment bytes one message may carry, all files together. Attachments are stored in the database until sent, and many mail servers refuse messages much above 10 MB.

properties.name: egradx.notification.max-attachments-per-message
properties.description: The most files one message may carry.

properties.name: egradx.notification.max-recipients-per-message
properties.description: The most addresses one {@code submit} may carry. Refused at the call site above this, so a mistake that would mass-mail thousands of people fails loudly instead. Raise it deliberately if an application genuinely sends that widely.

properties.name: egradx.notification.metrics.backlog-refresh
properties.description: How long a count of the delivery backlog is reused before the table is counted again. The count runs only when metrics are read, at most this often per instance.

properties.name: egradx.notification.preferences.channels
properties.description: The channels a person's notification settings offer, in order — those that reach a person, as opposed to a system (webhooks). Match egradx-auth's {@code egradx.auth.profile.channels}.

properties.name: egradx.notification.retention.cleanup-interval
properties.description: How often old deliveries and notifications are deleted.

properties.name: egradx.notification.retention.dead
properties.description: How long {@code DEAD} deliveries are kept — longer, since those are the ones someone investigates.

properties.name: egradx.notification.retention.in-app
properties.description: How long in-app notifications are kept, read or not. Without a limit, platform-wide notifications accumulate for ever, and every unread count scans all of them.

properties.name: egradx.notification.retention.sent
properties.description: How long {@code SENT} deliveries are kept.

properties.name: egradx.notification.schema.migrate
properties.description: Whether the library applies its own migrations at startup, into its own history table ({@code egradx_notification_schema_history}). Turn off only if the application creates these tables itself — from {@code db/egradx-notification/} in this jar.

properties.name: egradx.notification.secrets.passphrase
properties.description: Encrypts stored channel secrets. Defaults to {@code egradx.security.crypto.passphrase}. Changing it makes every stored secret unreadable until re-entered.

properties.name: egradx.notification.templates.compiled-cache-size
properties.description: How many compiled templates to keep in memory.

properties.name: egradx.notification.templates.locations
properties.description: The application's classpath template locations, searched in this order before the library's own ({@code classpath:egradx-notification/templates/}). Each must start with {@code classpath:}. See {@code EgradxClasspathTemplates} for the file layout.

properties.name: egradx.observability.correlation.enabled
properties.description: Give every HTTP request an id, in the MDC and on the response.

properties.name: egradx.observability.correlation.request-headers
properties.description: Headers a caller's request id is taken from; the first well-formed one wins.

properties.name: egradx.observability.correlation.response-header
properties.description: Header the request id is returned in.

properties.name: egradx.observability.logging.default-correlation-pattern
properties.description: Set {@code logging.pattern.correlation} to show trace, span and request ids on every log line, unless the application sets it itself. Read before the application context exists, so only from configuration files, the environment and the command line.

properties.name: egradx.observability.logging.shipping.batch-size
properties.description: The most lines sent together in one batch.

properties.name: egradx.observability.logging.shipping.enabled
properties.description: Whether log lines are shipped to an {@code EgradxLogSink}.

properties.name: egradx.observability.logging.shipping.excluded
properties.description: Logger name prefixes never shipped, besides the transports' own.

properties.name: egradx.observability.logging.shipping.flush-interval
properties.description: The longest a line waits before its batch is sent.

properties.name: egradx.observability.logging.shipping.max-error-length
properties.description: A logged exception's stack trace is cut at this length.

properties.name: egradx.observability.logging.shipping.minimum-level
properties.description: Lines below it are not shipped.

properties.name: egradx.observability.logging.shipping.queue-capacity
properties.description: Lines waiting to be sent; beyond it they are dropped and counted.

properties.name: egradx.observability.metrics.enabled
properties.description: Record egradx counters and gauges when the application has a MeterRegistry.

properties.name: egradx.redis.enabled
properties.description: Whether the libraries coordinate through Redis. Off, each instance counts, caches and pushes on its own.

properties.name: egradx.redis.key-prefix
properties.description: Starts every key and channel. Instances that must act together use the same prefix; applications sharing one Redis use different ones (contracts/redis).

properties.name: egradx.rest-template.connect-timeout
properties.description: How long to wait for a connection.

properties.name: egradx.rest-template.read-timeout
properties.description: How long to wait for data once connected.

properties.name: egradx.security.client.authorization-grant-type
properties.description: The grant to request, normally {@code client_credentials}.

properties.name: egradx.security.client.client-id
properties.description: This service's OAuth client id.

properties.name: egradx.security.client.client-secret
properties.description: This service's OAuth client secret.

properties.name: egradx.security.client.scope
properties.description: The scope to ask for with the service token. Not yet sent by the Java token manager, which requests the client's default scope; the Node SDK sends it.

properties.name: egradx.security.crypto.keystorePath
properties.description: The folder holding the signing and encryption keys; created with them on the first start. Every instance shares it. Written exactly so: it is read as written.

properties.name: egradx.security.crypto.passphrase
properties.description: Encrypts the private keys in the keys folder. Required; keep it stable and secret.

properties.name: egradx.service.token.enabled
properties.description: Creates the EgradxServiceTokenManager, which gets client-credentials tokens from an outside OAuth server (egradx.security.client.*).
